source.quote: SMSL's own page for the PS200, read 2026-11-27 with curl, « Introduction » bullets: « ESS new generation of high-end analog-to-digital conversion chips ES9039Q2M; »; « Brand-new 3rd generation XMOS XU-316, PCM support up to 32bit/768kHz, DSD Support to DSD512; »; « Input ports (excluding Bluetooth) support MQA and DSD, Coaxial and Optical support DoP64; »; « UAC1/2 mode switching, UAC1 can easily connect to SONY PS5, Nintendo SWITCH, etc; »

facts.chip: ESS ES9039Q2M, XMOS XU-316 on USB. The page calls it « analog-to-digital conversion chips », a slip for digital-to-analogue.

_the_ceiling_is_the_XMOS_bullet: The rate and DSD ceilings come from the bullet naming the XMOS USB receiver, so they are written on usb only. No other input is given a PCM rate: the page states none.
_optical_has_DoP64_and_no_rate: Optical and coaxial get DoP64 from the maker's own clause and no PCM ceiling, because none is stated: copying 768 kHz onto optical is the error vocabulary/why-the-optical-default-stays-low.json exists to prevent.
_UAC1_mode_lowers_the_ceiling: « UAC1/2 mode switching »: the recorded ceiling is the UAC2 one; the page gives none for UAC1.
